standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's Definition 5.1 at source lines 1441-1448 (printed Definition 5.1): for symmetric Psi in BS^0, [A] := [A]_Psi := exp(-i Psi) A exp(i Psi).

standard_prerequisites.name: The iterated commutator ad^k
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's recursive definition at source lines 775-782 (eq:defadk, printed (2.39)): ad^0(A;B) = A and ad^k(A;B) = ad(ad^{k-1}(A;B); B).
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement's series is written in ad^k; the proof's final display identifies ad^k(A;Psi) with k! times the sum of the (j,m)-terms with j+m=k.

standard_prerequisites.name: The product/norm estimate for operator products (Lemma 2.13, label lem:product)
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's lemma at source lines 732-738 (printed Lemma 2.13): for A in BS^alpha and B in BS^beta, AB in BS^{alpha+beta} with snorm{AB}{alpha+beta}{l} <= snorm{A}{alpha}{l} snorm{B}{beta}{l+|alpha|}.
standard_prerequisites.use: Step 1 of the proof invokes it ('Lemma 2.13 yields the bounds') to bound each product term Psi^j A Psi^m; the card cites it by its printed number only.

core_obligations: Step 1 (proof lines 1464-1467): the product lemma yields the bound snorm{Psi^j A Psi^m}{alpha}{l} <= (snorm{Psi}{0}{l})^j snorm{A}{alpha}{l} (snorm{Psi}{0}{l+|alpha|})^m for all l >= 0.

Step 2 (proof lines 1468-1471): the bracket is expanded into the double series [A]_Psi = sum_j (-i Psi)^j/j! A sum_m (i Psi)^m/m! = sum_{j,m} (-i Psi)^j/j! A (i Psi)^m/m!, and the product bounds show it converges absolutely in BS^alpha.
Step 3 (proof lines 1472-1475): recursively, ad^k(A;Psi) = k! sum_{j+m=k} (-i Psi)^j/j! A (i Psi)^m/m! for all k >= 0, closing the counted series with qedhere.
Conclusion (statement lines 1456-1460): [A]_Psi = sum_{k>=0} (1/k!) ad^k(A;Psi), and the series converges absolutely in BS^alpha.
proof_roadmap: Term-wise product bounds from the product lemma reduce every monomial Psi^j A Psi^m (proof lines 1464-1467).
Exponential double-series expansion of the bracket, dominated absolutely in BS^alpha by those bounds (proof lines 1468-1471).
Recursive identification of ad^k with the k-th diagonal of the double series, delivering the counted identity with absolute convergence (proof lines 1472-1475, statement lines 1456-1460).

The proof (proof lines 1463-1476) is a 13-line argument whose only input is the author's product/norm estimate (Lemma 2.13): term-wise bounds dominate the exponential double series, and a recursive rearrangement identifies ad^k with the k-th diagonal. H2: a short, standard absolute-convergence manipulation resting on one named estimate.

standard_prerequisites.name: The overlap function zeta(lambda; A)
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's definition at source lines 2796-2804 (eq:defnoverlap, printed (9.5)): zeta(lambda; A) is the maximal t >= 0 with [lambda-t, lambda+t] contained in one spectral band of A, and 0 off the spectrum.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both the statement's equality and the proof's identification of zeta(lambda; A) with zeta(lambda; A_+) appeal to this definition.

standard_prerequisites.name: Spectrum of a fibre-wise direct sum
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard spectral fact, used at proof line 2995: the spectrum of a direct sum is the union of the spectra of the summands, applied fibre-wise over the punch-hole torus.
standard_prerequisites.use: Step 2 of the proof localizes the high part of the spectrum of A(k) to the summand A_+(k).

standard_prerequisites.name: The framework classes of uncoupled elliptic almost-periodic systems
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's standing notation (BU BS^alpha_m, BS BE BS^alpha_m, and the fibration of periodic operators over the punctured torus) introduced in sections 2 and 6 of the article.
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement's hypotheses place A in these classes; the counted proof uses only the fibre decomposition A = A_+ + A_- with A_+ semi-bounded below and A_- semi-bounded above.

core_obligations: Step 1 (proof line 2991): since A_- is semi-bounded above, there is lambda_0 > 0 with spec(A_-) intersected with (lambda_0, infinity) empty.

Step 2 (proof lines 2992-2996): for every lambda > lambda_0 and every k in the punctured torus, spec(A_+(k)) intersected with [lambda, infinity) equals spec(A(k)) intersected with [lambda, infinity): the high part of each fibre spectrum is carried by the + summand alone.
Step 3 (proof line 2997): zeta(lambda; A) = zeta(lambda; A_+) for lambda > lambda_0 follows from the definition of the overlap function.
Step 4 (proof lines 2997-2998): replacing A by -A swaps the roles of the summands and yields zeta(-lambda; A) = zeta(-lambda; A_-) for lambda > lambda_0, after possibly increasing lambda_0.
Conclusion (statement line 2987): there is lambda_0 > 0 so that for every lambda > lambda_0, zeta(+/-lambda; A) = zeta(+/-lambda; A_+/-).
proof_roadmap: High-energy spectral localization: above lambda_0 the spectrum of each fibre of the direct sum comes entirely from the + summand (proof lines 2991-2996).
The overlap equality at large lambda is then a direct application of the definition of zeta (proof line 2997).
The mirrored statement at -lambda by running the same argument on -A (proof lines 2997-2998, statement line 2987).
task_snapshot.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a periodic direct sum with one summand semi-bounded below and the other semi-bounded above, the overlap function at large spectral parameter equals that of the corresponding summand (statement lines 2982-2988, printed 10.3). The proof (proof lines 2990-2999) is a 10-line spectral-localization argument: semi-boundedness removes the upper spectrum of one summand, the direct-sum spectrum identity localizes the high part of each fibre spectrum, and the overlap equality follows from the definition, with a mirrored argument for -A. H2: a short, standard argument whose content is the high-energy localization observation.

standard_prerequisites.name: The spectral bands iota_j and their epsilon-neighbourhoods
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's band notation: the j-th spectral band iota_j (source line 2793) of a periodic operator family, and the epsilon-neighbourhood I_{-eps} of an interval (source lines 2805-2810).

standard_prerequisites.name: Non-decreasing labellings of the discrete fibre eigenvalues
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The statement's hypothesis: for self-adjoint periodic operators with discrete fibre spectrum, a labelling lambda_j(A_p(k)) that is non-decreasing in j for each k.
standard_prerequisites.use: The closeness condition eq:evlabelclose compares the two operators' eigenvalues label-by-label; the argument transfers the interval inclusion from A_1 to A_2 through it.

core_obligations: Step 1 (proof line 2926): if 2 eps > zeta(lambda; A_1), the claimed inequality holds trivially from nonnegativity of the overlap function; otherwise proceed.
Step 2 (proof lines 2926-2930): choose j in Z such that [lambda - zeta(lambda; A_1), lambda + zeta(lambda; A_1)] is contained in the band iota_j(A_1).

Step 3 (proof lines 2931-2935): the closeness hypothesis eq:evlabelclose shrinks that band by eps on each side and lands it inside a band of A_2: [lambda - zeta + eps, lambda + zeta - eps] contained in iota_j(A_1)_{-eps} contained in iota_j(A_2).
Step 4 (proof line 2936): reading the definition of the overlap function off the inclusion yields zeta(lambda; A_2) >= zeta(lambda; A_1) - 2 eps.
Conclusion (statement lines 2919-2922): zeta(lambda; A_2) >= zeta(lambda; A_1) - 2 eps.
proof_roadmap: Trivial branch of the case split is disposed of by nonnegativity of zeta (proof line 2926).
The band of A_1 realizing the overlap maximum is shrunk by eps and transferred to A_2 through the label-closeness hypothesis (proof lines 2926-2935).
The final inequality is read off the definition of the overlap function (proof line 2936, statement lines 2919-2922).

The proof (proof lines 2925-2937) is a 13-line case split with a single interval-nesting argument transferring the maximal band of A_1 into a band of A_2. H2: a short, standard argument whose content is the eps-shrinkage transfer of the band inclusion.

standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's definition at source lines 3493-3496 (printed (11.50)): n(xi, E) = #{theta in Theta : xi + theta in E}, for xi in R^d and E a subset of R^d.

standard_prerequisites.name: The global resonant and non-resonant sets CZ and CG, and the symbol CZ'
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's definitions at source lines 3488-3491: CZ is the union of the resonant zones CZ_j and CG the union of the non-resonant zones CG_j. The primed symbol CZ' is invoked by the author in the statement without a definition anywhere in the article (the published text of Lemma 11.10 does the same); by the volume bound it carries, which matches the enlarged-zone estimate eq:volCZ of Lemma 11.6, it denotes the union of the enlarged resonant zones.

core_obligations: Step 1 (proof line 3510): for any subset E of R^d the counting function n(xi; E) is constant on the fibres xi mod Theta (it depends only on the fractional part of xi), hence is well defined on the punctured torus and N is Theta-invariant.
Step 2 (proof lines 3511-3515): vol(CN_CG) = integral over CN/Theta of n(xi; CG) d xi <= m times the integral of n(xi; CZ') = m vol(CN intersect CZ') <= m vol(CZ').
Step 3 (proof lines 3517-3518): the claim vol(CN_CG) << vol(CZ') << delta rho^{d-alpha-eps_0} follows from Lemma 11.6 (the enlarged-zone volume estimate with eps_0 = 1 - nu - d kappa).

The m-fold counting bound vol(CN_CG) <= m vol(CZ') is read off the same fibre integral (proof lines 3511-3515).
The upper bound on vol(CZ') is imported from the enlarged-resonant-zone estimate of Lemma 11.6 (proof lines 3517-3518, statement lines 3504-3507).

standard_prerequisites.name: The enlarged resonant zones and the distance margin (Lemma 11.6, label lem:enlargedresonant)
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's lemma at source lines 3289-3311 (printed Lemma 11.6): for xi in CG_j the distance from xi to every resonant zone CR_{j'} exceeds r rho^{1-nu}.
standard_prerequisites.use: Step 1 of the proof invokes it to obtain the margin r rho^{1-nu} that keeps the short radial segment inside the band.

standard_prerequisites.name: The eigenvalue branch decomposition and the gradient estimate (Lemma 11.5, label lem:descriptiongj)
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's lemma at source lines 3235-3259 (printed Lemma 11.5): g_j = a_j |xi|^alpha + G_j with G_j of class C^2 on the band CB_j and |nabla G_j| + rho |nabla^2 G_j| << rho^gamma for some gamma < alpha - 1.
standard_prerequisites.use: Step 2 of the proof invokes it ('By Lemma 11.5') to bound the derivative of the perturbation part G_j along the segment by rho^{gamma+1} = o(rho^alpha).

standard_prerequisites.name: The band regions CB_j and the primed symbol CB'_j
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's band definition at source line 3250: CB_j := CA_j \ CR_j, the part of the annular spectral region off the resonant zones. The primed symbol CB'_j is invoked by the author in the proof without a definition anywhere in the article (the published text does the same); by the margin estimate of Lemma 11.6 that precedes its use, it denotes the band region with the rho^{1-nu} margin in which the segment remains off resonance.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof locates the whole segment xi + t(xi + b), |t| <= t0, inside CB'_j before differentiating.

standard_prerequisites.name: The parameters kappa, Theta_kappa, nu and the angle phi
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's standing parameters fixed in Remark 11.4 (source lines 3223-3234), and phi(xi, xi+b) the angle between xi and xi+b; the hypothesis phi <= pi/4 gives cos(phi) > sqrt(2)/2.
standard_prerequisites.use: The margin exponent nu enters t0 = r rho^{-nu}, and the angle hypothesis drives the lower bound on the radial derivative in Step 3.

core_obligations: Step 1 (proof line 3473): since xi in CG_j, Lemma 11.6 provides r > 0 with dist(xi; R_{j'}) > r rho^{1-nu} for all j'; hence for |t| <= t0 := r rho^{-nu} the segment point xi + t(xi + b) stays in the band region CB'_j.
Step 2 (proof lines 3473-3476): by Lemma 11.5 the derivative of the perturbation part along the segment satisfies |d/dt G_j(xi + t(xi + b))| << rho^{gamma+1} = o(rho^alpha).

Step 3 (proof lines 3477-3484): the radial part satisfies d/dt |xi + t(xi + b)|^alpha = alpha |xi + t(xi + b)|^{alpha-2} (|xi| |xi+b| cos(phi) + t |xi+b|^2) >> rho^alpha, since cos(phi) > sqrt(2)/2 by the hypothesis phi <= pi/4.

Step 4 (proof lines 3484-3485 and statement lines 3462-3466): combining, the derivative d/dt g_j(xi + t(xi + b)) = a_j d/dt |xi + t(xi + b)|^alpha + d/dt G_j(...) is >> rho^alpha, so the branch is increasing on [-t0, t0] with derivative >> rho^alpha.

Conclusion (statement lines 3458-3469): for all xi in CG_j and all b with |xi + b| asymp rho and phi(xi, xi+b) <= pi/4 there is t0 >> rho^{-nu} such that for |t| <= t0 the point xi + t(xi + b) lies in CB'_j and the branch g_j is increasing with derivative >> rho^alpha; the implicit constant depends only on the functions g_j and the constants in |xi + b| asymp rho.
proof_roadmap: A distance margin from the enlarged-resonant-zone lemma localizes the short radial segment inside the band (proof line 3473, stub Lemma 11.6).

A competition of scales: the perturbation derivative is o(rho^alpha) by the gradient estimate, while the radial derivative of the main term is >> rho^alpha by the angle hypothesis (proof lines 3473-3484, stub Lemma 11.5).
The monotonicity and the lower bound on the derivative follow by summing the two contributions (statement lines 3462-3469).

The proof (proof lines 3472-3485) is a 14-line argument: a distance margin from the enlarged-resonant-zone lemma keeps the segment in the band, the perturbation derivative is o(rho^alpha) by the gradient estimate, and the radial derivative of the main term is >> rho^alpha by the angle hypothesis. H2: a short one-variable-calculus argument on top of two named estimates.

standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's lemma at source lines 3405-3414 (printed Lemma 11.8): for any omega in (0,pi) and eps > 0, if delta rho^{2-alpha+2eps} -> 0 then the volume of the union over i,j and over theta in Theta of CY'_{ij,omega}(theta) is << delta^2 rho^{4-2alpha+2d+6eps} + delta rho^{1-alpha+d-eps(d-1)}, with implicit constants depending only on delta, omega, Z and the coefficients a_j.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof's last step bounds vol(CU) by the volume of the union of the pi/8-angled crossing sets and substitutes this estimate at omega = pi/8 (proof line 3562, stub Lemma 11.8).

standard_prerequisites.name: The crossing sets CY_{ij}, CY_{ij,omega} and the prime convention
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's definitions at source lines 3382-3391: CY_{ij}(b) := CG_i cap (CG_j + b) and CY_{ij,omega}(b) := {xi in CY_{ij}(b) : phi(xi, xi-b) > omega}; the prime convention (source lines 3393-3402) rescales the delta parameter, CE'(delta) := CE(Z delta) for a large constant Z depending only on d, alpha and a_1,...,a_m.
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement defines CU through membership xi + theta_1 in CY'_{ij,pi/4}(theta_1 - theta_2), and the proof manipulates these sets by translation and by weakening the angle from pi/4 to pi/8.

standard_prerequisites.name: The good and resonant sets CG, CZ and the overlap set CN
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's definitions at source lines 3491-3494 (CG := union of CG_j, CZ := union of CZ_j) and in the preceding lemma's statement (source lines 3498-3501, CN := {xi in R^d : n(xi; CG) <= m n(xi; CZ')}, CN_CG = CN cap CG); n(xi;E) counts lattice elements theta with xi + theta in E (source lines 3496-3498).
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement locates CU inside CG \ CN, which partitions the good spectral region into the overlap part CN_CG (bounded by Lemma 11.10) and the crossing part CU (bounded here).

standard_prerequisites.name: The angle function phi and the lattice Theta
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's standing notation: phi(xi, eta) is the angle between the vectors xi and eta, Theta is the dual-period lattice of Section 11 and Theta-dagger its admissible subset of counting elements.
standard_prerequisites.use: The angle hypothesis phi(xi+theta_1, xi+theta_2) > pi/4 and the elementary bound max{phi(xi, xi+theta_1), phi(xi, xi+theta_2)} > pi/8 drive the inclusion of Step 3, and Theta-dagger supplies the lattice elements over which CU is quantified.

core_obligations: Setup (proof lines 3535-3537): take xi in CU, so xi in CG_k for some k, and lattice elements theta_1, theta_2 in Theta-dagger with xi + theta_1 in CY'_{ij,pi/4}(theta_1 - theta_2).
Step 1 (proof lines 3537-3540): by the definition of CY'_{ij,pi/4} and translation, xi lies in (CG_i' - theta_1) cap (CG_j' - theta_2).
Step 2 (proof lines 3541-3544): hence xi lies in CY'_{ki}(-theta_1) cap CY'_{kj}(-theta_2) by unwinding the definition of CY_{ij} with the shifted arguments.

Step 3 (proof lines 3545-3548): the crossing hypothesis gives phi(xi+theta_1, xi+theta_2) > pi/4, and the elementary inequality max{phi(xi, xi+theta_1), phi(xi, xi+theta_2)} > pi/8 follows since the two angles to xi sum to more than pi/4.
Step 4 (proof lines 3549-3552): combining Steps 2 and 3, xi lies in CY'_{ki,pi/8}(-theta_1) union CY_{kj,pi/8}(-theta_2).

Step 5 (proof lines 3553-3562): summing over all i,j and theta, vol(CU) <= vol(union of CY'_{ij,pi/8}(theta)), and Lemma 11.8 at omega = pi/8 yields vol(CU) << delta^2 rho^{4-2alpha+2d+6eps} + delta rho^{1-alpha+d-eps(d-1)} under the hypothesis delta rho^{d-alpha+2eps} -> 0.

Conclusion (statement lines 3528-3531): under the hypothesis delta rho^{d-alpha+2eps} -> 0 the good-crossing set CU has volume bounded by delta^2 rho^{4-2alpha+2d+6eps} + delta rho^{1-alpha+d-eps(d-1)}, with the implicit constant of Lemma 11.8 at omega = pi/8.
proof_roadmap: A membership translation: the crossing condition on xi + theta_1 is unwound by the definition of the crossing sets into a pair of shifted good-set memberships for xi itself (proof lines 3537-3544).
An angle bookkeeping: the pi/4 crossing angle forces one of the two angles at xi to exceed pi/8, upgrading the pair of memberships to a single pi/8-angled crossing membership (proof lines 3545-3552).

A volume bound: covering CU by the union of the pi/8-angled crossing sets and invoking the total-intersection estimate (Lemma 11.8) gives the stated two-term bound (proof lines 3553-3562, stub Lemma 11.8).

The proof (proof lines 3534-3563) is a 30-line chain: membership in CU is translated by the definition of the crossing sets into shifted good-set memberships, an elementary angle inequality upgrades the angle from pi/4 to pi/8, and the volume bound follows by covering CU with the pi/8-angled sets and invoking the total-intersection estimate Lemma 11.8. H2: a geometric inclusion chain on top of one named estimate, with no new analytic input.

standard_prerequisites.name: The lattice Theta and its admissible subset Theta-dagger

Step 1 (proof lines 3417-3425): by Proposition 11.7 there are constants c and C depending on omega, delta, T and the numbers a_j such that vol(union over theta of CY'_{ij,omega}(theta)) is at most the sum over theta with c rho <= |theta| <= C rho of vol(CY_{ij,omega}(theta)), which is << delta^2 rho^{4-2alpha+2d+6eps} + delta rho^{1-alpha+d-eps(d-1)}.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Clifford algebra F_{p,q}, its generators gamma_j and the grading Gamma
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's conventions at source lines 3684-3712: gamma_1,...,gamma_d and Gamma are matrices satisfying the Clifford relations (the gamma_j square to the identity, anticommute pairwise, and anticommute with the grading operator Gamma, which squares to the identity); the odd subspace is spanned by products of an odd number of generators.
standard_prerequisites.use: The computation u o u^dagger = Id uses gamma_j gamma_k xi_j xi_k = delta_{jk} xi_j^2, Gamma^2 = Id and gamma_j^2 = Id (proof lines 3809-3819), and the final symbol |xi| Gamma lands in the odd subspace.

standard_prerequisites.name: The matrix symbol classes BS_m^beta and DBES_m^1
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's standing classes: BS_m^beta is the matrix-valued symbol class of order beta, DBES_m^1 its diagonal elliptic subclass of order 1, and BS_m^{-infty} the smoothing class (source lines 1855-1900 and Section 3).
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement places U in BS_m^0, U A_d U^* in DBES_m^1 and the remainder R in BS_m^{-infty}; the proof exhibits their symbols explicitly.

core_obligations: Step 1 (proof lines 3802-3807): by (2.30) the symbol of U^dagger is u^dagger(x,xi) = the same expression as u with the sign of the i/|xi| term flipped.

Step 2 (proof lines 3808-3819): the composition u o u^dagger equals 1_{|xi|>=1}/2 (Id_m - |xi|^{-2} sum_{j,k} Gamma^2 gamma_j gamma_k xi_j xi_k) + 1_{|xi|<1} Id_m, which by the Clifford relations collapses to sum_j gamma_j^2 xi_j^2 = |xi|^2 and hence to Id_m; so U is unitary.
Step 3 (proof lines 3820-3823): in the same fashion the conjugated symbol is [u o a_d o u^dagger](xi) = 1_{|xi|>=1} |xi| Gamma + 1_{|xi|<1} a_d(xi).

Step 4 (proof lines 3824-3828): take R in BS_m^{-infty} with symbol r(xi) = 1_{|xi|<1}(a_d(xi) - |xi| Gamma); then the symbol of U A_d U^* - R is |xi| Gamma, which is diagonal, elliptic of order 1 and valued in the odd subspace, proving U A_d U^* in DBES_m^1.

Conclusion (statement lines 3797-3798): the operator U with symbol (eq:explicitunitary) is unitary, U A_d U^* in DBES_m^1, and there is R in BS_m^{-infty} such that the symbol of U A_d U^* - R is |xi| Gamma.
proof_roadmap: A unitarity check: composing the explicit symbol with its adjoint (2.30) and using the Clifford relations collapses every non-scalar term, so u o u^dagger = Id (proof lines 3802-3819, context (2.30)).
A conjugation computation: the same Clifford algebra bookkeeping diagonalizes the conjugated symbol to |xi| Gamma outside the unit ball (proof lines 3820-3823).
A smoothing remainder: the low-frequency discrepancy is absorbed into R in BS_m^{-infty}, leaving the diagonal elliptic principal symbol |xi| Gamma (proof lines 3824-3828).

standard_prerequisites.name: The permitted-perturbation conjugation (Proposition 12.9, label prop:permittedperturbations)
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's proposition at source lines 3852-3862 (printed Proposition 12.9): for scalar perturbations B_Id, B_Gamma, B_j of order beta < 1 the conjugated operator U(A_d + B)U^* equals Op(|xi|) Gamma plus an uncoupled part B' in BUBS_m^beta, an odd-subspace part tilde B in BS_m^beta and a remainder R in BS_m^{beta-1}.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof's opening invokes it to check the hypotheses of Theorem 8.1 for the conjugated operator (proof line 3945, stub Proposition 12.9).

standard_prerequisites.name: The restricted asymptotic expansion theorem (Theorem 8.1, label thm:aexpconcretecut)
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's theorem at source lines 2410-2418 (printed Theorem 8.1): for a pd operator with subprincipal part in BS_m^beta, beta <= alpha/2, satisfying Conditions I-IV and the multiplicity condition with gamma* = max(2 beta - alpha, gamma), the IDS has the two-term restricted asymptotic expansion with exponents d-j and remainder O(rho^{d-1+gamma*}).
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof imports its conclusion verbatim at alpha = 1, where gamma* = max{beta - 1, 2 beta - 1} (proof lines 3945-3947, stub Theorem 8.1).

standard_prerequisites.name: The Dirac setting and the Clifford perturbation ansatz
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's conventions of Section 12: A_d = sum_j gamma_j d/dx_j is the free Dirac operator on spinors, m(d) the spinor dimension, and B = B_Id Id_m + B_Gamma Gamma + sum_j B_j gamma_j the scalar Clifford-coefficient perturbation ansatz fixed in the statement.
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement fixes the class of perturbations to which Theorem 8.1 is transported after the conjugation of Proposition 12.9.

core_obligations: Step 1 (proof lines 3945-3946): by Proposition 12.9 the conjugated operator U A U^* satisfies the hypotheses of Theorem 8.1 with gamma* = max{beta - 1, 2 beta - 1} and alpha = 1.
Step 2 (proof lines 3946-3947): the restricted asymptotics of the IDS given in Theorem 8.1 therefore hold for such operators with alpha = 1.

Conclusion (statement lines 3936-3941): for beta <= 1/2 and B in the Clifford ansatz satisfying Conditions I-IV, putting gamma* = max{beta - 1, 2 beta - 1}, there is a finite set L subset (0, 1 - gamma*) and constants such that N^+(A; lambda) = C_0^+ lambda^d + sum_{j in L} sum_{q=0}^{d-1} C_{j,q}^+ lambda^{d-j} log^q lambda + o(lambda^{d-1+gamma*}), and similarly for N^-.
proof_roadmap: A conjugation transfer: the permitted-perturbation proposition converts the perturbed Dirac operator into an uncoupled principal part plus controlled remainders, checking the hypotheses of the restricted expansion theorem (proof line 3945, stub Proposition 12.9).
A parameter import: the expansion is read off Theorem 8.1 at alpha = 1 with gamma* = max{beta - 1, 2 beta - 1} (proof lines 3946-3947, stub Theorem 8.1).

proof_roadmap: A symbol-level inversion: the regularization congruence plus the ellipticity lower bound give a pointwise symbol bound, hence a convergent Neumann-type inverse in DES^{-alpha} and the norm estimate (proof lines 921-932).

standard_prerequisites.name: The commutator norm estimates (2.41) and (2.42)
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's estimates at source lines 792-796 and 799-801 (printed (2.41) and (2.42)): the multi-commutator norm is bounded by 2^k times the product of the factor seminorms, and the zero-order specialisation bounds ad^k(A;B) by 2^k times the product of the A and B seminorms.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof's opening applies both to derive the k-step estimate (5.25) (proof lines 1615-1621, stubs (2.41) and (2.42)).

standard_prerequisites.name: The gauge symbol and its estimates (Lemma 5.5 with (5.19), (5.20), (5.21))
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's Lemma 5.5 at source lines 1578-1587 with the definitions and estimates (5.19) at 1570-1576, (5.20) at 1580-1582 and (5.21) at 1584-1586: psi^{delta,s} defined by (5.19) is a symbol of order gamma-delta, its quantization Psi satisfies the norm bound (5.20) and the modified commutator identity (5.21).
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof uses the Psi norm bound inside the k-step estimates and the identity for the odd-subspace chain (proof lines 1622-1635, stubs Lemma 5.5, (5.19), (5.20), (5.21)).

standard_prerequisites.name: The remainder definition and the resonant-part estimate ((5.8) and (5.18))
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's definitions at source lines 1490-1492 and 1559-1561: R is defined by (5.8) as the first commutator plus the exponential series, and (5.18) bounds the resonant and regular parts by the full off-diagonal part.
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement quantifies over this R and the proof's final step derives the R bounds from (5.8) with (5.26), (5.27) and (5.18) (proof lines 1636-1637, stubs (5.8) and (5.18)).

core_obligations: Step 1 (proof lines 1615-1621): from (2.41), (2.42), delta > gamma and Lemma 5.5 derive the k-step commutator estimate (5.25) for ad^k(A^COD; Psi); choosing k = 1 gives the statement's first bound (5.23).
Step 2 (proof lines 1622-1630): from (5.20) derive the bound (5.26) on ad^k(A^CD; Psi).
Step 3 (proof lines 1631-1635): from (5.21) derive for k at least 2 the bound (5.27) on ad^k(A^CD; Psi) via ad^{k-1}(A^CNR; Psi).

Conclusion (proof lines 1636-1637 and statement lines 1602-1612): the R norm bounds (5.24) follow from (5.8), (5.26), (5.27) and (5.18); ad(A^COD; Psi) and R are symmetric and lie in S^{beta+gamma-delta}.

Step 3 (proof lines 2671-2687): by Theorem 6.4 the quasi-periodic A is unitarily equivalent, through conjugation with exp(i Psi), to A' + R = A^D + Y + R (local eq (4)), where the conjugator symbol is the explicit fraction (local eq (5)) with the indicator chi_{j,k}; using ad(A; Psi) = ad(A^{OC}; Psi) - A^{NR}, the remainder R is obtained from (6.35), (6.36) with tilde R = 0 and (6.37) as the four-term display (local eq (6)).

Step 4 (proof lines 2689-2701 and statement lines 2644-2655): by Lemma 4.12 the perturbation gives the two-sided interval comparison (local eq (7)) with eps = the operator norm of R; the commutator contribution is bounded by Corollary 2.9 and Lemma 2.13 as in Proposition 2.16 (local eq (8)), the third and fourth terms of (6) use the same estimate plus absolute convergence, and the first term B^{R,C}, of order gamma and supported where |xi| > c rho, is bounded by Proposition 2.16 (local eq (9)); together these give eps much less than rho_n^{gamma^*}, which completes the proof of the statement.
proof_roadmap: A double reduction: the uncoupled asymptotic proposition reduces the errorest display to the interval comparison, and the quasi-periodicity lemma strips the frequency-set complexity (proof lines 2659-2670).

A gauge normal form: the one-step gauge theorem conjugates A to a diagonal plus remainder form with an explicit conjugator, and the gauge recursion displays write the remainder concretely (proof lines 2671-2687).

Norm bookkeeping: interval-count monotonicity transfers the remainder to a two-sided interval comparison, and three symbol-norm estimates bound the remainder's contributions, closing eps much less than rho_n^{gamma^*} (proof lines 2689-2702).
